newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks ride bonds to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks ride bonds to higher close.

text.p: The Australian share market closed higher on Wednesday with buying picking up pace in the afternoon as local bonds took heart from Japanese economic data that eased concerns about a possible interest rate tightening there.
The All Ordinaries index rose 21.9 points to 2,284.2.
September share index futures rose 18 points to 2,284, and were at a 0.2 point discount to the underlying index.
Brokers said that with Wall Street up and metals prices looking to be holding well, the afternoon boost from bonds gave the bourse a late fillip.

"Wall Street was better and with metals prices holding most books were on the buy side," said broker Martin Angel of brokerage Eyres Reed, noting that afternoon interest was spread across the board, not just concentrated among the leaders.
"It flowed through to the smaller end as well," he said.
Others players agreed, citing a market chock-full of notable performances in a variety of sectors
Among the golds, Lihir jumped on news that its Papua New Guinea mine would come on stream earlier than expected.
The mine is expected to produce 175,000 ounces in calendar 1997 despite only operating from October 1997.
News Corp was the best performer among the leaders, jumping on a combination of ADR strength flow-on and value seekers after a sharp selloff following its results last week.
Shares of food ingredients group Burns Philp fell after the company announced a full year net loss of A$61.8 million and said it would not pay a final dividend.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about 10 to seven, while about 34 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
